title: Positive profinite Cech exactness for norm-topological algebraic scalars
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] with its extended nonarchimedean norm topology, and use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A profinite set means a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space. For a continuous surjection $q:T\to V$ of profinite sets and $n\geq0$, put
$$T_V^{n+1}=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_n)\in T^{n+1}:q(t_0)=\cdots=q(t_n)\},\qquad C^n(q)=C(T_V^{n+1},\Omega),$$
with the subspace topology and all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Give these additive groups the differential
$$(d^nf)(t_0,\ldots,t_{n+1})=\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^jf(t_0,\ldots,\widehat{t_j},\ldots,t_{n+1}).$$
The following is the corrected noncomplete-coefficient statement.

(1) Global positive exactness fails in general: there exist nonempty metrizable profinite $T,V$, a continuous surjection $q:T\to V$, and $f\in C^1(q)$ with $d^1f=0$, such that there is no $g\in C^0(q)$ with $d^0g=f$.

(2) The split-cover and local replacement holds in every positive degree. If $q$ has a continuous section $\sigma:V\to T$, then for every $n\geq1$ and $f\in C^n(q)$ with $d^nf=0$, the formula
$$g(t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})=f(\sigma(q(t_0)),t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})$$
defines a continuous $g$ with $d^{n-1}g=f$. For an arbitrary $q$, let $q':T\times_VT\to T$ be the first projection. The pullback of $f$ to the nerve of $q'$ has the continuous primitive
$$h(s;t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})=f(s,t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1}),$$
where all displayed points have the same $q$-image. Thus this positive exactness is valid after the profinite base change $T\to V$. The empty surjection is included in (2). All equalities concern the actual $\Omega$-valued functions, without completion, closure of images, or finite-subextension-valued replacement.

proof.text: Choose $q:T\to V$ and $t_k^\pm$ from [lem-sfb-countable-split-profinite-cover]. Apply [lem-sfb-algcl-countable-closed-finite-cover] with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ to obtain increasing closed finite intermediate fields $F_k$ exhausting $\Omega$. These choices retain the nonempty metrizable profinite spaces and all the clopen-pair and tail-density properties.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-algcl-small-escaping-sequence] choose $a_k\notin F_k$ with $|a_k|\leq\ell^{-k}$ and $a_k\to0$. Take $A=(\Omega,+)$ with norm $|\cdot|$ and $H_k=(F_k,+)$: the extended norm is ultrametric, and each closed field contains zero and is closed under differences. Step 1 supplies the remaining hypotheses of [lem-sfb-double-fibre-null-cocycle-obstruction]. Its function $f$ is continuous, satisfies $d^1f=0$, and has no continuous $g:T\to\Omega$ with $g(y)-g(x)=f(x,y)$. The coordinate homeomorphism $T_V^1\to T$, $(t_0)\mapsto t_0$, with inverse $t\mapsto(t)$, identifies this last equation with $d^0g=f$. This proves (1).

proof.text: For a continuous section $\sigma$ of $q$, apply [lem-sfb-split-topological-cech-homotopy] to the additive topological group $\Omega$. For $d^nf=0$ its identity gives $d^{n-1}(h_nf)=f$. Its formula for $h_n$ is exactly the displayed $g$ in (2), with continuity included.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-created analytic auxiliary; the blueprint motivates but does not state the noncomplete Cech assertion. Repair assembly, step 3

proof.text: For arbitrary $q$, [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-fiber-product] makes $P=T\times_VT$ profinite with its subspace topology. The first projection $q':P\to T$ has the continuous diagonal section $s\mapsto(s,s)$, hence is surjective. A tuple over $q'$ is $((s,t_0),\ldots,(s,t_n))$, identified with $(s;t_0,\ldots,t_n)$ where all $q$-images agree. Both identifications are continuous coordinate maps. The coordinate map forgetting $s$ pulls $f$ back to $F(s;t_0,\ldots,t_n)=f(t_0,\ldots,t_n)$; deletion of any $t_j$ commutes with it, so $dF=0$. Applying [lem-sfb-split-topological-cech-homotopy] to $q'$ and its diagonal section gives $h(s;t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})=f(s,t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})$ and $dh=F$. If $T=V=\varnothing$, every positive-length tuple space is empty and the same formulas are the unique zero functions. This proves the base-change assertion of (2).
